This looks like late 2016. Unemployment is 5.0%, fed funds is about 0.41%, and the 10-year yield is 1.86%, which fits a point after the November 2016 election. Headline CPI at 1.48% and core at 2.21% fit as well. The 3m change in the policy rate (+0.11) points to the funds rate moving from about 0.30 to 0.41, which matches October 2016 to November or December 2016.

Unemployment was 4.9% in October 2016 and 4.7% in November, so 5.0% with a +0.10 3m change doesn't fit those months exactly. It matches 5.0% in September 2016 (it was 5.0% in Sept, 4.9% in Oct). The 10-year at 1.86% fits end-October 2016, when it was about 1.83%, but the 3m change of +0.40 implies the yield was about 1.46 at the end of July. That fits a late-October reading, and the 20y+ Treasury return of -4.4% in 1m fits too. The funds rate of 0.41 fits October 2016 (0.40). The VIX at 16.19 fits the end of October. The S&P fell 1.7% in October, which matches. Gold fell 2.9% in October, which also matches.

Unemployment of 5.0% may have been the September value, since October data was not published until early November. That fits a snapshot taken at the end of October.
